headline: Cannabis calendar: the US deadlines from 12 November to 23 December
dek: Hemp bans, a DEA supply-chain deadline, licensing windows in five states and the Aurora takeover vote all land before year-end. Here is what each date decides.
key_points: The federal hemp rewrite arrives in two steps: synthetic cannabinoids leave the hemp definition on 12 November, and the 0.4 mg total THC per container cap follows on 11 December unless Congress acts.
DEA guidance expects medical operators with temporary federal authorisation to have compliant supply chains by 29 November, and comments on 2027 marijuana production quotas close on 10 December.
Licensing windows close or open in Georgia (16–20 November), Rhode Island (23 November) and Los Angeles (4 December lottery), with California hearing split-licence rules on 15 December.
For investors, Curaleaf's Aurora offer expires on 4 December and Aurora votes on Organigram's deal on 23 December.
body: The last seven weeks of 2026 are crowded for the US cannabis business. Federal hemp rules change in two stages, the Drug Enforcement Administration's first compliance deadline under rescheduling arrives, several states open or close licence windows, and courts and regulators hold hearings that will shape 2027. The Marijuana Herald published a list of 15 policy dates on 11 November; MetaFlora has checked those dates against our own reporting and primary sources where we could, added the market dates we track, and grouped them by what they decide.

Two notes before the list. First, several of these dates can still move: Congress can change the hemp deadline, and courts can grant or deny injunctions. Second, this is a guide to the calendar, not to what any business should do; operators should rely on their own counsel and the regulators' texts.
## Hemp: two federal steps and three state fights

On 12 November, the first piece of the revised federal hemp definition takes effect: products containing cannabinoids that the plant cannot produce naturally no longer count as hemp. Congress delayed the rest of the rewrite to 11 December, but kept this provision on the original date. Missouri's own law moving intoxicating hemp products into licensed dispensaries also begins on 12 November, as we reported on 11 November.

On 19 November, US District Judge Martha Pacold is scheduled to hear a request for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction against Illinois's new hemp law, which limits most intoxicating hemp products to licensed dispensaries and sets a 0.4 mg total THC limit per container. Illinois has agreed not to enforce the law against the plaintiffs and covered association members until that hearing, as we reported on 10 November.

On 11 December, the rest of the federal rewrite is scheduled to take effect, bringing stricter limits on THC-containing hemp products, including a 0.4 mg total THC limit per container for certain final hemp-derived cannabinoid products. The Senate's draft farm spending bill for fiscal 2027 keeps that date, as we reported on 12 November. On 15 December, Massachusetts' Cannabis Control Commission must deliver its study and recommendations on regulating hemp-derived products, including THC drinks, under a state law enacted in April.
> The hemp calendar runs in one direction: by mid-December most intoxicating hemp sales will either be inside a licensed system or in a courtroom.
## Federal rescheduling: the DEA's first deadlines

On 29 November, state-licensed medical businesses operating under temporary federal authorisation are expected to have compliant supply chains, under DEA guidance described by The Marijuana Herald. In practice, businesses with timely registration applications must generally buy Schedule III medical marijuana only from other timely applicants or DEA registrants. The guidance is non-binding, and the DEA is letting some inventory acquired earlier stay in use. The same agency has already begun moving to deny some applicants, as we reported on 12 November, so this deadline will show how strictly the supply-chain rule is applied.

On 10 December, comments close on the DEA's proposed 2027 production quotas, which keep the Schedule I marijuana quota at 6,675,000 grams and the marijuana extract quota at 1 million grams, while separate quotas for Schedule III products are being developed. We covered the proposal on 9 November. On 19 November, the US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces hears United States v. Lawrence, on whether the legal inference used to prosecute service members for THC use is constitutional.

Georgia's Access to Medical Cannabis Commission takes dispensary applications from existing licensed producers from 16 to 20 November, with the patient registry near 65,000. Rhode Island's Cannabis Control Commission closes its adult-use retail application portal at 16:00 Eastern on 23 November, and majority owners of applicants must complete background checks by 4 December. Vermont's event-sales pilot takes applications from 16 to 30 November, with a lottery on 16 December. Missouri's research facility licensing rules take effect on 30 November, and new provisions of Connecticut's Public Act 26-8, letting licensed hemp manufacturers make CBG, CBN and other approved cannabinoids for the regulated market, start on 1 December.

Los Angeles holds its retail storefront licensing lottery for qualifying social equity applicants on 4 December. California's Department of Cannabis Control holds a hearing on 15 December on rules letting businesses with combined medical and adult-use licences split them through an expedited process, a step tied to federal medical registration; 95 businesses have already done so under emergency rules. Washington's Liquor and Cannabis Board has three dates: a comment deadline on 4 December for a medical operator certification proposal, a 10 December hearing on financial interest agreements for retailers, and a 17 December hearing on rules letting producers form cooperatives of up to three licences.

In Michigan, both cannabis taxes moved to a new state portal on 12 November, and all 2026 quarterly wholesale marijuana tax returns are due on 20 January 2027, according to the state Treasury. In markets, Curaleaf's hostile offer for Aurora Cannabis expires on 4 December unless extended, and Aurora shareholders vote on Organigram's agreed C$7.80-a-share takeover on 23 December, with 18 November as the record date.

The two dates with the widest effect are 29 November and 11 December: the first tests how the DEA polices medical supply chains under Schedule III, and the second decides how much of the hemp THC market survives outside licensed dispensaries. Congress can still amend or delay the hemp date before 11 December; absent action, it stands. MetaFlora will report each date as it happens.
